source.title: Understanding the Effects of Pre-Training for Object Detectors via Eigenspectrum
source.authors: Yosuke Shinya; E. Simo-Serra; Taiji Suzuki

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains object detectors from random initialization on COCO and reports training dynamics and performance outcomes, bearing on scratch-training and training-schedule aspects of V1. It does not report training classification error or the benchmarks and model-size comparisons specified by V1.
record.gate_note: The paper reports eigenspectrum measurements during training and COCO validation accuracy, not training classification error. The cited claim that scratch-trained Mask R-CNN can be on par with fine-tuned models is prior work, not a result of this study. The paper's own reports of similar COCO AP, learning-schedule effects, and eigenspectrum dynamics are included where relevant; architecture search results are not treated as training-error outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses established initialization and normalization recipes to analyze pre-training and develop detector architectures. Its own outcomes are validation AP, ImageNet evaluation error and feature-covariance eigenspectra. None measures the training-error, local-minimum, depth, initialization-speed, stability-threshold or batch-normalization effects specified by V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors find that similarly accurate scratch-trained and fine-tuned detectors have different intrinsic architectures, and propose eigenspectrum-based width selection that reduces parameters while preserving validation AP. They argue that current fine-tuning methods inadequately retain useful ImageNet features and that better knowledge-transfer methods are needed. Their schedule-based explanation of overfitting is interpretive, not a direct measurement of training-error or stability-threshold claims.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates object detection and instance segmentation training on COCO, with Group Normalization and ResNet-50-based detectors, and measures feature eigenspectra and validation AP rather than training classification error on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Training schedule changes reported COCO AP; the paper reports 1× versus 2×/3× schedules, and eigenspectrum counts rebound after learning-rate decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Scratch-trained and fine-tuned Mask R-CNN models attain similar validation AP while retaining different higher-layer feature eigenspectra.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similar detector validation accuracy can coexist with different representations depending on pre-training.

fits_no_version.finding: Eigenspectrum-derived width architectures preserve detector validation AP with fewer parameters; their relative AP also depends on training schedule.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-covariance eigenspectra can guide parameter-efficient detector width allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: Architectures derived from different detector training histories transfer differently to ImageNet classification.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effectiveness of a learned width allocation depends on the evaluation task and its source model.

fits_no_version.finding: Some feature-covariance eigenvalue counts rebound after learning-rate decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate decay can coincide with increased feature representation dimensionality.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.1 reports 0.5 percentage points lower COCO AP for DetNet-59 with He normal initialization than with the default PyTorch initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization choice can affect final detector validation AP.

record.peer_reviewed: 2019 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshop (ICCVW)
record.problems: The paper does not measure training classification error, so the outcomes cannot determine whether the claim's predicted near-zero training error occurs. Main reported performance is COCO validation AP. Table 1 includes a mean of five runs for the marked backbone rows and a significance test for one comparison, but uncertainty is not provided for most reported results.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows were omitted. Cited prior-work results, including the reported scratch-trained Mask R-CNN parity from [19], are not included as this paper's own results.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including CIFAR benchmarks, corrupted labels and model-size or regularization conditions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth. Appendix A.1's initialization comparison reports final detection AP only.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, recovery and divergence.
Controlled batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No version receives a verdict. The study is not an original source for these versions, but its reported measures do not test them. Architecture-method performance rows should not be treated as optimization-claim evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, or model-size thresholds. Its training results concern object detection and instance segmentation on COCO.
